facts.title: Student finance applications open (2028/29)
facts.text: Applications for student finance for courses starting in autumn 2028 are expected to open in spring 2028 (around March). You don't need a confirmed university place to apply. From courses starting on or after 1 January 2027, England uses the new Lifelong Learning Entitlement (LLE) system.

personalStatement.appliesTo: 2026 entry onwards (so it covers 2028 entry unless UCAS announces a change)
personalStatement.format: Three questions, answered in separate boxes
questions: Why do you want to study this course or subject?
How have your qualifications and studies helped you to prepare for this course or subject?
What else have you done to prepare outside of education, and why are these experiences useful?
personalStatement.text: The UCAS personal statement is three questions with a 4,000-character limit in total (including spaces) and at least 350 characters per answer. You can split the 4,000 characters however you like, and admissions staff read the three answers as one statement.

source.evidence: Each answer will have a minimum character count of 350 characters, which is clearly labelled on the question boxes, along with an overall character counter, so you can keep track.

extraSources.evidence: Applying for university or college to start your studies from 2026 onwards? Find out more about the personal statement format and tips on what to include.
The 4,000 overall character limit (including spaces) remains the same, as does what you're expected to include.
Question 1: Why do you want to study this course or subject?
Question 2: How have your qualifications and studies helped you to prepare for this course or subject?
Question 3: What else have you done to prepare outside of education, and why are these experiences useful?
Admissions staff will still review your personal statement as a whole

polarChecker.name: Young participation by area: search by postcode (Office for Students)
polarChecker.quintiles: Quintile 1 = lowest rate of young people going into higher education, quintile 5 = highest.

predictedGrades.text: Predicted grades are set by your school or college and added to your UCAS application with your reference, after you submit it to them by their internal deadline. UCAS advises schools to give students their likely predicted grades early enough to research courses, and predictions must be final by the time the application is sent. UCAS doesn't set a national date: your school decides when (often after Year 12 assessments).

source.evidence: students should be given their likely UCAS predicted grades in time to inform their research about which courses and providers may be suitable choices for them.

extraSources.evidence: Finalised by the point of submitting an application – universities and colleges may only consider the predicted grades received as part of the UCAS application.
If your referee is one of your teachers, they can add your predicted grades for any pending qualifications you’re studying now.

notConfirmed: UCAS publishes no fixed date for predicted grades; timing is set by each school (the 'often after Year 12 assessments' remark is UCAS's 'ideally before any assessments that may inform them' guidance, not a date)

openDays.text: UCAS doesn't publish a national open-day season: each university sets its own dates, listed in UCAS's open-day search. UCAS advises Year 12s to visit at least two open days, to book (most need booking) and to contact universities some months ahead because days get booked up. UCAS's suggested sixth-form calendar: spring of Year 12 for researching options, summer of Year 12 for making decisions and starting the UCAS application.

source.evidence: If possible, Year 12s thinking about going to university should visit at least two open days.

extraSources.evidence: Top tip: Remember that most open days require pre-booking, so preparation is key
Open days and campus visits: Make sure you contact the university you wish to visit some months ahead as days get booked up.
Spring Year 12: Researching options Event title: What and where to study?
Summer Year 12: Making decisions Event title: How to complete your UCAS application
Use the open days search tool to find out when the university they’re interested in is holding its next open day.

notConfirmed: No official UCAS statement on when open days usually happen (months); check each university's open-day page

studentFinance.text: In England, courses starting on or after 1 January 2027 are funded through the new Lifelong Learning Entitlement (LLE) student finance system, so 2028 entry uses LLE. You don't need a confirmed offer to apply, and you must reapply each year of your course.

source.evidence: For courses starting on or after 1 January 2027, you may need to apply for student finance through the new student finance system. The new system is called your Lifelong Learning Entitlement (LLE).

extraSources.evidence: You will need to apply for funding for each course you study. If your course lasts longer than a year, you will need to reapply each year of your course.
